invariants: Control identity survives revision, reassignment, implementation change and assessment turnover.
Every effective control references exactly one immutable approved revision.
Control existence, documentation, implementation or policy status never proves effectiveness.
Effectiveness requires an external scoped assessment with evidence, method, conclusion time and validity.
A risk may rely on a control only through an explicit assessment-context citation.
Residual-risk reduction requires a current effectiveness determination covering the relied-on mechanism and scope.
A missing, expired or invalidated determination makes reliance unknown rather than effective.
Execution occurrences and telemetry remain external evidence and never become control revisions.
One control cited by multiple risks never merges those risk identities or assessments.
Superseding or retiring a control revision marks dependent assessment contexts stale without rewriting history.
Control ownership and assessment authority remain separately attributable.
Retired control identifiers remain resolvable and are never recycled.
